claims.claim: The set S = {0} ∪ A ∪ [50,∞), where A = {25,26,28,30,31} ∪ [38,48] and intervals contain integers, is a numerical semigroup.
claims.evidence: S contains zero and consists of nonnegative integers. Every positive element is at least 25, so any two positive elements sum to at least 50 and hence belong to S. Addition by zero preserves membership. Every integer at least 50 belongs to S, proving finite complement.
claims.search_method: Exact prefix enumeration and a complete closure argument using the defined infinite tail.

claims.claim: S has multiplicity 25, Frobenius number 49, and genus 33.
claims.evidence: Exact enumeration below 50 gives minimum positive member 25 and precisely 33 gaps, with maximum 49. The defined tail excludes any further nonnegative gaps.
claims.witness: The complete gap set is [1,24]∪{27,29,32,33,34,35,36,37,49}; its cardinality is 24+9=33.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive integer membership enumeration below the conductor.

claims.claim: The complete minimal positive generating set of S is A.
claims.evidence: Every element of A is below 50 and cannot be a sum of two positive elements of S. Exhaustive decomposition checks show every member from 50 through 74 is decomposable. For every n≥75, n=25+(n−25), with both summands positive in S. Strong induction therefore proves A generates S, and indecomposability forces every element of A into every generating set.
claims.witness: E={0,1,3,5,6} satisfies E+E=[0,12], providing decompositions of [50,62]. For 63≤n≤73 use 25+(n−25); use 74=26+48. The checker prints a decomposition for every integer from 50 through 74.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive tests of all positive two-summand decompositions below 75, verification of the submitted additive identity, and induction covering the infinite tail.

claims.claim: S satisfies the source's leaf hypothesis.
claims.evidence: The source defines a leaf by requiring every minimal positive generator to be at most F. The complete minimal generating set is A, whose maximum is 48, while F=49.
claims.search_method: Comparison of every independently established minimal generator with the Frobenius number under the exact supplied definition.

claims.claim: The nine gaps H = {27,29,32,33,34,35,36,37,49} are pseudo-Frobenius numbers.
claims.evidence: Every listed integer is a gap. For every x∈H and every positive s∈S, x+s≥27+25=52≥50, so x+s∈S. This covers every positive semigroup element.
claims.search_method: Exact gap verification and a uniform inequality proving the universal addition condition.

claims.claim: The seven gaps P = {13,14,15,16,17,20,22} are pseudo-Frobenius numbers.
claims.evidence: All listed integers are gaps. Put D={25,26,28,30,31}. For 13≤x≤17, x+D⊆[38,48]. Also 20+D={45,46,48,50,51} and 22+D={47,48,50,52,53}, all in S. Every positive s∈S outside D is at least 38, so x+s≥51 for every x∈P.
claims.witness: P={13,14,15,16,17,20,22}, with the complete finite addition checks printed by the checker.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive addition tests below the conductor threshold, independently cross-checked against all minimal generators; larger addends are covered by the tail inequality.

claims.claim: There are no pseudo-Frobenius numbers outside H ∪ P.
claims.evidence: Every remaining positive gap has the explicit obstruction recorded in the witness. For x≤−26, adding 25 gives a negative integer outside S. For −24≤x≤−1, adding 25 gives a gap in [1,24]. For x=−25, adding 26 gives the gap 1. Zero and all other nongaps belong to S and are excluded by definition. These cases exhaust Z\S.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive testing of all 33 positive gaps using the exact cutoff s<50−x, verification of every obstruction, and a complete three-case exclusion of negative integers.

claims.claim: The type of S is exactly 16.
claims.evidence: The complete pseudo-Frobenius set is H∪P. These disjoint sets have cardinalities 9 and 7, respectively, giving type 16 under the source's definition over Z\S.
claims.search_method: Exact cardinality of the exhaustively certified pseudo-Frobenius set, with agreement between conductor-based and generator-based computations.

claims.claim: S refutes the exact recorded conjecture.
claims.evidence: S is a numerical semigroup satisfying the exact leaf hypothesis and has genus 33≥2. Euclidean division gives 33=4·8+1. The conjecture therefore requires type at most 2·8−1=15, whereas the independently certified type is 16.
claims.witness: The specified S has (g,q,r,F,t)=(33,8,1,49,16), all minimal generators at most 48, and 16>15.
claims.search_method: Verification of every source hypothesis and exact integer evaluation of the applicable conjectured bound.

target_evidence: The exact original conjecture is false. The independently verified witness is a numerical semigroup whose complete minimal positive generating set has maximum 48≤F=49, satisfying precisely the source's leaf definition. Its genus is 33≥2 and its type is 16. Since 33=4·8+1, the conjectured bound is 15, which is strictly violated. The finite computations have complete logical reductions covering all larger integers, all positive addends, and all negative pseudo-Frobenius candidates. Thus every hypothesis and the violated conclusion are established, and the draft's claimed FULL resolution is accurate.
